questions.prompt: At 20–30 big blinds, suited connectors are worth less because…

choices.text: You cannot win a deep implied-odds pot when you flop a monster.
Short stacks make every draw the nuts

questions.explanation: Implied odds need chips behind. A short stack is paid off less when the draw gets there.

questions.prompt: Hands that are ahead right now, such as offsuit broadways and pairs, …

choices.text: Go up in value. You are often committed if you continue.

questions.explanation: Low stacks reward current equity, not speculative flop potential.

questions.prompt: Under about 20 big blinds, a small open you hate folding is often replaced by…

choices.text: Checking your option before cards are dealt

questions.explanation: There is no room for a raise and a fold. Decide for the stack before you put chips in.

choices.text: A mistake. The payoff is too small when you flop the set.
The best use of a short stack

questions.explanation: You need a deep stack behind the raiser to make small pairs profitable as calls.
